title: Service of the heart (Taanit 2a)
hookLine: the Talmud calls prayer the service of the heart

cards: The Shema, said morning and evening, includes a paragraph from Deuteronomy asking people to serve God with all their heart. Serve how? You can serve with your hands: build, carry, cook, bring an offering to an altar.
That's what service meant in the Temple, real physical work. But you can't hand someone your heart on a plate. The Talmud stops at that phrase and asks exactly that question.

teach.b: The verse is Deuteronomy eleven: "to love the LORD your God, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul." At the opening of tractate Taanit, the Talmud asks: what is service that is in the heart?
Its answer: this is prayer. Avodah shebalev, service of the heart.

Avodah is the same word used for the priests' work in the Temple: the offerings, the incense, the daily routine. So the phrase makes a bold claim. Prayer is real service, standing alongside the Temple's.
After the Temple was destroyed, that idea carried enormous weight: there was still a service anyone could bring, every day, with no altar at all. And the heart?
The rabbis learned much about prayer from Hannah, at the start of the book of Samuel, praying for a child.
"Now Hannah, she spoke in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice could not be heard."
From her, the Talmud learns that prayer needs the heart directed, the lips moving, and the voice kept low. Directing the heart has its own word: kavanah, intention.
The siddur supplies the words; the heart does the work of meaning them. That's why it's called service. It isn't only a feeling.
It's effort, like any other work.

how: Jewish law asks for kavanah, focused intention, especially in the first line of the Shema and the first blessing of the Amidah, which is said quietly, lips moving, in the manner learned from Hannah.

o: love for God felt without any words at all

games.q: the Talmud reads 'serve Him with all your heart' and asks: what is service with the heart? what's its answer?
games.why: Taanit 2a: 'this is prayer'. the same word as the Temple service, done with the heart.

practice: Let one honest sentence rise in you: thanks, a worry, a hope, a name. Say it the way Hannah did, lips moving, voice barely there, then once more, slower, meaning every word.
If you pray, it can be to God in your own words; if not, say it to the quiet.
